title: ORM forgets attribute after lazy loading relationship (and emits a spurious COMMIT)

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

body:
**Describe the bug**
I found a bug (or 2?) with sqlalchemy 1.4.6 that happens when lazy loading a relationship.
It seems that the lazy loading will wipe an attribute on the model that I just set, and it will also emit a COMMIT statement without a reason to.
SQLAlchemy 1.3.19 instead works as expected.

**Expected behavior**
A COMMIT statement should not be issued when accessing a relationship, and the attribute should stay as set before.

**To Reproduce**
```python3
from sqlalchemy import *
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship, sessionmaker


Base = declarative_base()

engine = create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:', echo=True)


class Foo(Base):
    __tablename__ = "foo"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

    important_attribute = Column(String(40), index=True, unique=True)

    bar_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("bar.id"))
    bar = relationship("Bar")


class Bar(Base):
    __tablename__ = "bar"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)()


foo = Foo()
session.add(foo)
session.commit()

foo.important_attribute = "something_important"
assert foo.important_attribute == "something_important"

print("Going to access foo.bar...")
foo.bar  # Triggers COMMIT and resets `foo.important_attribute` to None
assert foo.important_attribute == "something_important"  # AssertionError: foo.important_attribute is None

```
